reference_use.conclusion:
The snapshot pins project 63436ae6 and Mathlib 25730c7c. Its Contract.lean is byte-identical to the workspace Contract and Submission.

What the snapshot already provides:
- Varifold.weight = measure.map Prod.fst, with weight_apply on measurable sets (SimonGMT Chapter08/Varifold.lean).
- Mathlib lemmas valid for arbitrary sets and functions, with no σ-finiteness: Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ (μHE[d](r•s) = ‖r‖₊^d•μHE[d] s for every s), MeasurableEquiv.smul₀ / coe_smul₀, Set.preimage_smul₀, Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff₀, MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map, lintegral_map_equiv, Measure.restrict_congr_set and Measure.restrict_apply (measurable test set, arbitrary restricting set).
- Also present: NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq, lintegral_eq_zero_iff', setLIntegral_measure_zero and Measure.restrict_eq_zero.

What is missing (no match in Mathlib or SimonGMT):
- No change-of-variables lintegral lemma for Hausdorff measure under dilations. SimonGMT has only simonHausdorffMeasure_smul, a wrapper of the set-level Mathlib lemma.
- No varifold rescaling-of-representation lemma.
- No carrier dilation-invariance lemma.
- Mathlib's setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae₀ needs a null-measurable integration set, so it does not cover child C.

The pinned Mathlib deprecates Set.mem_setOf_eq (use Set.mem_ofPred_eq) and Set.diff_eq (use Set.sdiff_eq).

proof:
Source: the change-of-variables paragraph of parent Step 5 (B6), specialised to an arbitrary set D and integrand f. That paragraph reads: "For every set E, H(σ⁻¹(E)) = H(s⁻¹ • E) = s^{-n}·H(E). So H.map σ = ofReal(s⁻¹)^n • H, i.e. H = ofReal(s)^n • H.map σ. MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map holds for arbitrary sets … Then lintegral_map_equiv gives …".

Notation. H := (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) and c := ENNReal.ofReal. Fix s > 0, D and f.

1. The dilation. Since s ≠ 0, σ := MeasurableEquiv.smul₀ s (ne_of_gt hs) is a measurable equivalence of Euclidean N with σ w = s • w for all w. This holds definitionally (MeasurableEquiv.coe_smul₀). For every set E, σ⁻¹(E) = {w | s • w ∈ E} = s⁻¹ • E (Set.preimage_smul₀ with s ≠ 0).

2. Pushforward of H. Claim: H.map σ = c(s⁻¹)^n • H. By Measure.ext it is enough to test a measurable set E.
 - (H.map σ)(E) = H(σ⁻¹ E), by Measure.map_apply since σ is measurable.
 - By step 1 this is H(s⁻¹ • E).
 - By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ n (inv_ne_zero _) E, which holds for every set, this is ‖s⁻¹‖₊^n • H(E).
 - Since s⁻¹ ≥ 0, the coercion of ‖s⁻¹‖₊ into ℝ≥0∞ equals c(s⁻¹) (rewrite with ← enorm_eq_nnnorm, then Real.enorm_eq_ofReal).
 - So, using ENNReal.smul_def and ENNReal.coe_pow, the value is c(s⁻¹)^n · H(E) = (c(s⁻¹)^n • H)(E) (Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul).

3. Inversion. c(s)^n • H.map σ = c(s)^n • (c(s⁻¹)^n • H) = (c(s)·c(s⁻¹))^n • H = c(s·s⁻¹)^n • H = c(1)^n • H = H. This uses smul_smul, mul_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_mul (s ≥ 0), mul_inv_cancel₀, ENNReal.ofReal_one, one_pow and one_smul. Hence H = c(s)^n • H.map σ.

4. Pull out the constant. Rewrite the measure on the left-hand side only (e.g. conv_lhs => rw [h3]), because H also occurs inside H.map σ. Then ∫⁻_D f dH = ∫⁻_D f d(c(s)^n • H.map σ) = c(s)^n · ∫⁻_D f d(H.map σ), by Measure.restrict_smul, lintegral_smul_measure and smul_eq_mul.

5. Restriction commutes with the equivalence. For the arbitrary set D, (H.map σ).restrict D = (H.restrict (σ⁻¹ D)).map σ (MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map). No measurability of D is needed because σ is a measurable equivalence.

6. Change of variables. For the arbitrary function f, ∫⁻ f d((H.restrict (σ⁻¹ D)).map σ) = ∫⁻_{σ⁻¹ D} f(σ w) dH(w) (MeasureTheory.lintegral_map_equiv). No measurability of f is needed.

7. Conclusion. Steps 4–6 give ∫⁻_D f dH = c(s)^n · ∫⁻_{σ⁻¹ D} f(σ w) dH(w). Since σ⁻¹ D = {w | s • w ∈ D} and σ w = s • w definitionally, this is ∫⁻ x in D, f x ∂H = ENNReal.ofReal s ^ n * ∫⁻ w in {w | s • w ∈ D}, f (s • w) ∂H. No σ-finiteness of H was used; H^n on ℝ^N is not s-finite when n < N. ∎
